key_insight: LLM agents can act as a practical natural-language interface for home energy scheduling, achieving near-MILP performance when connected to real pricing, weather, solar, and usage tools.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a deployable path for lower-friction residential demand response and appliance optimization without requiring users to specify technical scheduling constraints.
method: Built a tool-calling ReAct agent with live Octopus Agile tariffs, weather forecasts, PV estimates, household usage data, and retrieval-augmented knowledge.
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth across tariff, conflict, and solar co-optimization scenarios.
Compared native function calling with text-parsed actions, and tested week-long simulated deployment savings versus an off-peak timer baseline.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark days and simulations, native function calling yielded 100% scheduling success and 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings, with projected annual savings of about GBP 1,270.
watch_item: Results depend on reliable tool integration and live data access; text-parsed action interfaces substantially reduce reliability and constraint handling.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
